correctness.rationale: The firing condition (closed same > opposite) gives nondecreasing cut; balancing both cliques is always allowed. For every uncut matched edge, either an endpoint gives strict gain or one neutral flip creates a strict gain, by the k+1-versus-k pigeonhole argument for odd or even n. Repetition reaches the global maximum. Classifying legal moves at maximum cuts proves all even states absorbing, and odd matched bits fixed with connected products of adjacent Boolean ranks. Exact binomial sizes and a two-new-unmatched-vertex bijection prove the parity identity. 25 exhaustive SCC instances and 42 independent bitset census instances verify boundaries but are not substitutes for all-size reasoning.

value.rationale: An exact family-wide attractor classification for two dense communities coupled by a variable partial matching: cross-links pin individual spins, changing odd recurrent-class multiplicity, while appending one unmatched vertex per clique preserves exactly the recurrent population but freezes every recurrent transition. The parity correspondence is a structural bijection, not a numerical coincidence; this precise geometry and its dynamical mechanism are motivated by anti-coordination on community graphs.
